reflections.title: "Give Thanks to the LORD"

reflect.text: When King Jehoshaphat faced an overwhelming enemy, he made an unusual choice. Instead of putting armed soldiers first, he placed an unarmed choir at the front line to sing praises to the Lord. Instead of giving in to anxiety or relying on human weapons, the king chose worship. Turning to praise in the middle of our troubles shifts our eyes away from fear and focuses our hearts on God's goodness.

It is easy to thank God after a struggle is over, but thanking Him before the fight begins shows real faith. Jehoshaphat praised God for deliverance while the danger was still right in front of him, trusting that God would keep His word. We can bring that same confidence into our mornings and our prayers. Starting with praise shows that we expect God to bless and help us.

Genuine worship carries spiritual power that changes the atmosphere of our lives. The moment Judah began to sing, the Lord intervened, causing the enemy forces to turn on one another and defeat themselves. When we put praise ahead of our own striving, we make room for God to display His power and fight on our behalf.

questions: When you face a difficult situation, do you tend to turn to worry or to praise?
What is one struggle you can thank God for handling before you see the outcome?
reflections.prayer: Lord, teach us to worship You even when we feel surrounded by difficulties. Help us to lay down our self-reliance and trust Your enduring love. Give us the faith to thank You for Your help before the victory arrives. Amen.

D2.author: Rick Warren
D2.work: How to Show Faith and Gratitude in Your Battle
